originalTitle: Bloom Energy CEO: Power Demand Is Coming From All Angles
summary: Bloom Energy marked its 25th anniversary by ringing the New York Stock Exchange opening bell, just days after joining the S&P 500, and used the moment to highlight its role in powering AI infrastructure. CEO K.R. Sridhar said Bloom's on-site power systems are becoming a standard solution as demand rises for data centers, factories, and hospitals. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close."
content:
Bloom Energy marked its 25th anniversary by ringing the New York Stock Exchange opening bell, just days after joining the S&P 500, and used the moment to highlight its role in powering AI infrastructure. CEO K.R. Sridhar said Bloom's on-site power systems are becoming a standard solution as demand rises for data centers, factories, and hospitals. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close."

You've come a long way, uh, KR. I mean, we talk about a company that, uh, I guess at one point was basically taking electricity and trying to turn it into oxygen, and now you're kind of doing the reverse. And of course, you've become the darling out there, basically the biggest bet right now on one of the biggest constraints in the AI space and that's electricity.

That's right. And uh we are so excited that our technology has established itself, become a standard for onsite power generation exactly at the time where market needs a lot of onsite generation. So, we are we are scaling and we are able to meet the growing demands of the AI data center, not by increasing the costs for a rate payer, not by polluting the air, not by using excess water, not by creating noise, but with a clean energy system that is manufactured in America using natural gas, but with the lowest emissions possible and powering reliably data centers and factories and hospitals. Uh we're super excited. We had all our manufacturing employees on the podium and on the floor uh for them to be able to see how their hard manufacturing work is translating to what it means to the market. And also, it's a great opportunity for us to show that we can power factories in America and bring manufacturing jobs back here. So, we're super excited.

Well, well let's talk about the manufacturing. I I think uh you've uh said that you intended to double your manufacturing capacity, the annual manufacturing capacity to about two gigawatts by the end of 2026. A, is that still on track? And more importantly, looking further out from 2026, um, what do you think that true sort of manufacturing capacity can be assuming you can get the supplies that you need?

Look, our goal when when we started the company 25 years ago was to power the planet. Even today, I'll tell you, we are on that path and we have a sense of urgency about it. So 2 gigawatts, think of that as the end of the year goal that we will get to, but we will continue to grow. The statement we have made is we will grow our manufacturing capacity as fast as the demand comes in. So as greater demand comes in, by the time a big factory can be built or by the time a big data center can be built, we would have scaled up the capacity and gotten them the power. We will not be the constraint for America's growth, either in manufacturing and factories or reliable hospitals or data centers. So, think of our expansion capacity as purely what the market needs. We believe the market need is very high, which means we will be growing very fast.

Are you confident in the spending, uh particularly by the hyper scalers, uh and some of the projections that are out there that those projections will indeed come true? Uh any concern about any potential slowdown or diversion of that spending?

Look, at the rate at which data centers are growing, could there be bumps along the road in terms of a slight slow down, the answer may be yes. But in reality is AI going to grow and is it going to require a lot more electricity, the answer is yes. But think about electrification of vehicles. 65% of all the cars made in China last year were EVs. That's happening globally. That requires a lot of electricity. Look at the number of factories that we are building today with robotics, with with controls that are all digitized. Look at the amount of electricity being used in every home today for so many applications we didn't have before. So, we don't think there is any any worry about electricity demand in the world slowing down or going down. Look at the amount of air conditioning that's being needed in so many places that don't have air conditioning. So the demand for power is coming from so many different angles. AI is just the big catalyst right now, but the demand is really secular for the next decade as far as I can see it.

On on the AI front though, I mean, obviously we know the demand is there. There are still a lot of questions about the supply bottlenecks, bottlenecks that go well beyond uh just what Bloom provides. And I do have to ask you about Project Jupiter, the force majeure notice uh from Oracle and whether that's altered at all uh any of your manufacturing plans related to that facility.

Look, unlike the other big power plants, our boxes are fungible. They can be installed in one location, or after we ship the unit while they are on the trucks, we can redirect the trucks to go to some other location and be able to operate. This is very different from conventional engines and turbines. For that reason, number one, we believe that when you have a portfolio of construction projects that we are supporting, some construction projects will come in, some will be on schedule, some will get delayed. But we have enough of a portfolio that we are confident in the numbers we project. So the guidance we have given for the year, uh which is greater than $4 billion, we will be able to meet and we are very confident about our growth next year too.

Well how broad is your portfolio though? I mean, your most recent filing uh suggested that about three quarters of your second quarter revenue came from uh one particular customer. So how broad is your portfolio beyond that customer?

We do have, we do have a very broad portfolio and we mentioned, we have we have we've given numbers in in in terms of customer and concentration risk, but financial investors who we call as a customer like Brookfield are really not the end customer. They are a large financier of our projects. So don't misread what we write about that being a customer. Br
chineseTitle: Bloom Energy首席执行官：电力需求来自各个角度
chineseSummary: Bloom Energy 在加入标准普尔 500 指数几天后，在纽约证券交易所敲响了开市钟，庆祝成立 25 周年，并利用这一时刻强调其在为人工智能基础设施提供动力方面的作用。首席执行官 K.R. Sridhar 表示，随着数据中心、工厂和医院需求的增长，Bloom 的现场电力系统正在成为标准解决方案。他在“The Close”节目中与罗曼·博斯蒂克进行了交谈。
chineseContent:
Bloom Energy 在加入标准普尔 500 指数几天后，在纽约证券交易所敲响了开市钟，庆祝成立 25 周年，并利用这一时刻强调其在为人工智能基础设施提供动力方面的作用。首席执行官 K.R. Sridhar 表示，随着数据中心、工厂和医院需求的增长，Bloom 的现场电力系统正在成为标准解决方案。他在“The Close”节目中与罗曼·博斯蒂克进行了交谈。

你已经走了很长一段路，呃，KR。我的意思是，我们谈论的是一家公司，呃，我想在某一时刻基本上是利用电力并试图将其转化为氧气，而现在你正在做相反的事情。当然，你已经成为那里的宠儿，基本上现在最大的赌注是人工智能领域最大的限制之一，那就是电力。

这是正确的。我们非常兴奋，我们的技术已经确立，成为现场发电的标准，而正是在市场需要大量现场发电的时候。因此，我们正在扩展，我们能够满足人工智能数据中心不断增长的需求，不是通过增加纳税人的成本，不是通过污染空气，不是通过使用过量的水，不是通过制造噪音，而是通过在美国使用天然气制造的清洁能源系统，但排放量尽可能低，并可靠地为数据中心、工厂和医院供电。呃我们非常兴奋。我们让所有制造员工都站在讲台上和地板上，让他们能够看到他们辛勤的制造工作如何转化为对市场的意义。而且，这对我们来说也是一个很好的机会，可以证明我们可以为美国的工厂提供电力，并将制造业就业机会带回美国。所以，我们非常兴奋。

好吧，让我们谈谈制造。我想，呃，你说过，你打算在 2026 年底之前将制造能力增加一倍，年制造能力达到约 2 吉瓦。 A，这还在轨道上吗？更重要的是，展望 2026 年，假设您能够获得所需的供应，您认为真正的制造能力是多少？

看，我们 25 年前创办公司时的目标是为地球提供动力。即使在今天，我也会告诉你，我们正走在这条路上，而且我们对此有紧迫感。所以 2 吉瓦，将其视为我们将达到的年终目标，但我们将继续增长。我们的声明是，我们将随着需求的增加而尽快提高我们的制造能力。因此，随着需求的增加，当可以建造大型工厂或大型数据中心时，我们就会扩大产能并为他们提供电力。我们不会成为美国增长的制约因素，无论是在制造业和工厂，还是可靠的医院或数据中心。因此，我们的扩张能力纯粹是市场需要的。我们相信市场需求非常高，这意味着我们将发展得非常快。

您对支出有信心吗，特别是超大规模的支出，以及一些预测，这些预测确实会实现吗？呃，是否担心该支出可能会放缓或转移？

看看数据中心的增长速度，一路上是否会出现稍微放缓的坎坷，答案可能是肯定的。但实际上，人工智能是否会发展，是否会需要更多的电力，答案是肯定的。但想想车辆的电气化。去年中国制造的所有汽车中有 65% 是电动汽车。全球范围内都在发生这种情况。这需要大量的电力。看看我们今天使用机器人技术建造的工厂数量，其控制装置都是数字化的。看看今天每个家庭用于许多我们以前没有的应用的用电量。因此，我们认为无需担心世界电力需求放缓或下降。看看许多没有空调的地方需要多少空调。所以对电力的需求来自很多不同的角度。人工智能目前只是一个重要的催化剂，但据我所知，未来十年的需求确实是长期的。

不过，在人工智能方面，我的意思是，显然我们知道需求的存在。关于供应瓶颈仍然存在很多问题，这些瓶颈远远超出了 Bloom 提供的范围。我确实必须询问您有关木星计划的情况、甲骨文发出的不可抗力通知以及与该设施相关的任何制造计划是否发生了改变。
